title: Arborline Diagnostics - Onboarding Immersion Session
summary: Kickoff immersion focused on Arborline's production timeline, networking and security constraints for PHI workloads, Dedicated capacity sizing for inference at 500 qps peak, and next steps to run a 2-week pilot. Redwood team to share SOC2 docs, pilot pricing, and a small benchmark plan.
action_items: Maya - send SOC2 & security pack + KMS integration notes - due 2025-05-02
Carlos - propose Dedicated GPU pool sizing and expected latencies for 512-token average inference - due 2025-05-05
Samir/Jenna - provide sample traffic profile and example prompt traces (anonymized) - due 2025-05-04
Elise - schedule 30-min pilot kickoff call (benchmarks) for the week of 2025-05-12 - due 2025-05-06
next_steps: Redwood to share runbook + security pack (link in notes)
Customer to confirm pilot scope and sample dataset for benchmarking
Set up VPC peering / private deployment checklist if customer opts for Private deployment
Follow-up demo of dedicated autoscaling controls and rollout policies
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Carlos Ortega, Elise Park (Redwood) — Dr. Lina Patel, Samir Rao, Jenna Morales, Omar Nadeem, Priya Singh (Arborline)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time this afternoon. quick goal for today — get aligned on onboarding runway, security constraints for PHI, and pilot sizing. i'll kick it off — maya from redwood inference, ae.
[00:14] Dr. Lina Patel: great, thanks maya. lina here. we're excited, we've been looking at the redwood docs and the numbers look promising. main ask is: can we keep inference inside our VPC because of PHI?
[00:28] Maya Chen: yes. we have a private deployment option — the private control plane or on-prem bundle. we also offer dedicated pools which can be VPC-isolated. carlos, want to add network detail?
[00:36] Carlos Ortega: sure. from an infra angle, we can run Dedicated inside your VPC via private endpoints. typical pattern: a customer provisioned subnet, peering, and then we accept a few security groups. there's also a small agent for telemetry if you want audit logs streaming to your splunk or s3. couple of caveats: egress rules and KMS key policies need to be set so the HSM/KMS calls succeed.
[00:54] Omar Nadeem: for compliance, we need to know whether keys remain customer-managed and if audit logs are tamper-evident. SOC2 documentation?
[01:05] Elise Park: yes — we will send the SOC2 report and our compliance pack. keys can be customer-managed with KMS integrations; the logs can be exported to your log archive. note: in the private mode the control plane endpoints are reachable only from the VPC, and we support bring-your-own-KMS.
[01:25] Samir Rao: curious on performance — we expect bursty qps up to 500 for our triage endpoint, avg payload ~512 tokens. what's latency like on Dedicated vs hosted? also thoughts on batching + KV cache for dialogs.
[01:40] Carlos Ortega: good question. ballpark: for a 512-token average, on an A100-like node with proper batching you'll see p95 around 220-280ms for the model variant we recommend. hosted has similar numbers but shared tenancy may add jitter; Dedicated gives more predictable SLOs. KV cache — we use prefix/KV caching to avoid recomputing context, that helps conversational workloads; sometimes the transcriber wrote it as K-V cash in docs — ha.
[02:07] Jenna Morales: and cost? at scale we have to optimize unit cost — does redwood give batching/quantization recommendations?
[02:13] Maya Chen: yes, our Optimize toolkit provides model and quantization suggestions and intelligent batching configs based on traces. carlos can propose quantization profile (int8 / mixed) depending on your quality tolerance.
[02:25] Carlos Ortega: right. the tradeoff matrix: int8 quantization reduces cost ~30-45% with small quality delta on many models; we can run a quick eval set. if you need deterministic outputs for clinical triage we might prefer a FP16 or mixed config.
[02:41] Dr. Lina Patel: clinical triage requires very high recall, we can't accept regressions. we'll want evaluation before rolling out quantization.
[02:49] Maya Chen: absolutely — we'll run prompt-set evals and quality-monitoring with regression alerts tied to your test prompts.
[02:55] Priya Singh: what's the simplest pilot scope to validate latency, cost, and accuracy?
[03:01] Elise Park: typical pilot: 2 weeks, limited set of endpoints (triage + summarization), synthetic or anonymized sample traffic, and a couple of evaluation prompt sets. Redwood provides a benchmark harness and a shared spreadsheet that tracks token counts, latency, and cost.
[03:16] Samir Rao: on networking, can we do a canary deploy across region fallback? we need to failover to non-PHI region when capacity is constrained.
[03:25] Carlos Ortega: yes, smart routing can do policy-based routing by region or cost tier. for PHI you'd keep the VPC-only route primary and a fallback to a dedicated-but-non-PHI cluster in another region — but note data residency rules if PHI leaves region. we'll document fallbacks in the runbook.
[03:44] Omar Nadeem: what about penetration testing and attestation — do you support pen test windows?
[03:50] Maya Chen: we can coordinate a pen-test window for the private deployment; there are standard guardrails and a process to notify infra teams. we'll include the process in the security pack.
[03:59] Dr. Lina Patel: okay let's talk timeline — we'd like pilot in mid-may and production by end of june if all goes well. is that realistic?
[04:08] Maya Chen: yes — mid-may pilot is feasible. immediate next steps are: redwood share security pack + runbook, customer share sample traces and traffic profile, redwood propose Dedicated sizing and pilot pricing.
[04:20] Carlos Ortega: on sizing: to hit 500 qps peak with 512-token avg and keeping p95 under 300ms, i estimate a 4-node Dedicated pool with 2x A100 equiv per node and autoscale headroom for burst. i'll put numbers in writing with expected cost per hour and per-token estimates.
[04:37] Jenna Morales: will you include estimates for both int8 and fp16 so we can compare cost and accuracy impact?
[04:43] Carlos Ortega: yes — int8 vs fp16, plus a fallback model with smaller context window to compare.
[04:50] Priya Singh: any gotchas with data retention and logs for PHI? we need guaranteed purge policies.
[04:56] Elise Park: we support configurable retention and purge hooks; in Private deployments we can disable persistent transcript storage and push logs into your archive under your retention policy.
[05:06] Dr. Lina Patel: awesome. quick question — will we get token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards?
[05:11] Maya Chen: yes — the Redwood Console gives per-route token breakdowns, latency heatmaps, and per-token cost. we'll share screenshots in the runbook link.
[05:20] Samir Rao: any known limits on number of concurrent streams or websocket connections for streaming responses?
[05:26] Carlos Ortega: we support continuous streaming; concurrent connections scale with the Dedicated pool, but there are per-connection rate limits and client-side throttles. we'll share recommended SDK configs to avoid head-of-line blocking.
[05:40] [brief cross talk — nobody audible]
[05:45] Maya Chen: ok to recap and assign owners?
[05:48] Dr. Lina Patel: yes please.
[05:50] Maya Chen: recap: 2-week pilot mid-may — scope: triage + summarization endpoints, anonymized sample traffic. action owners: maya will share SOC2 + security pack; carlos will send Dedicated sizing and cost estimates incl int8/fp16 options; samir/jenn a to provide sample traces; elise will schedule the pilot kickoff. we also agreed to run evals before any quantization. any additions?
[06:12] Jenna Morales: include an acceptance criteria doc for production — error budget, p95 SLO, and quality thresholds.
[06:18] Maya Chen: will do.
[06:20] Omar Nadeem: we'll also want a list of ACLs and required IAM roles to provision for peering. can you include that?
[06:25] Carlos Ortega: yes, that will be part of the VPC checklist.
[06:29] Maya Chen: great. thanks everyone — we'll send the pack and follow up.
[06:35] Dr. Lina Patel: thanks all.
[06:38] End of recording.

References shared during call: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/arborline-pilot (runbook link), Security pack (SOC2) — shared via gated link in follow-up, Benchmark sheet: /shared/benchmarks/arborline-pilot.xlsx

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., quantization transcribed 'quantisization', 'K-V cash' for KV cache), some speaker labels simplified.
